page: Microsoft Azure D4a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled, consisting of a 102 GB local SSD, and the virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core and parallelized execution metrics are notably weaker. Multi-core performance in stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark falls into the bottom 25%, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is mixed, showing average read-only speeds for large blocks of 40.46 GB/sec but weak write speeds of 24.31 GB/sec and weak cached small-block reads. Cryptographic operations perform at an average level, as evidenced by the Passmark CPU encryption test.

The qualitative cost profile of the D4a_v4 reflects a budget-friendly entry point for dedicated AMD EPYC resources, offering a bundled local SSD that reduces the need for immediate external storage attachments. The primary tradeoff is the disparity between its strong single-threaded performance and its limited multi-threaded scaling. Consequently, this server is best suited for workloads that do not heavily parallelize, such as lightweight web serving, single-threaded data processing, basic text processing, or development environments. It is less optimal for heavy database operations, parallel software compilation, or multi-threaded high-performance computing.

Benchmarks reveal a strong single-core CPU performance (top 25% in stress-ng), contrasted by weaker multi-core scaling and memory write bandwidth, which fall into the bottom 25%. It is best suited for general-purpose tasks, lightweight web serving, single-threaded data processing, and development environments.
